title: Trolley: the switch
dilemma: A runaway trolley will kill five workers unless you pull a lever that diverts it onto a side track, where it will kill one worker. Should you pull the lever?
tension: Outcomes (save five) versus the duty not to cause a death.

title: Trolley: the footbridge
dilemma: You can stop a runaway trolley headed for five people only by pushing a large stranger off a footbridge onto the track, killing him. Should you push him?
tension: Same numbers as the switch case, but using a person merely as a means.

title: Whistleblowing on a safety cover-up
dilemma: An engineer learns her employer hid test results showing a product can fail dangerously. Reporting it will likely cost hundreds of colleagues their jobs. Should she go to the regulator?
tension: Public safety and honesty versus loyalty and harm to colleagues.

title: Lying to protect a friend
dilemma: A man with a knife asks where your friend is hiding so he can hurt her. Should you lie to him?
tension: Kant's famous hard case: the duty not to lie versus protecting life.

title: Keeping a promise to a dying friend
dilemma: You promised a dying friend to give his savings to his estranged son, who you now learn will likely spend it on gambling. A local hospice desperately needs funds. What should you do?
tension: Promise-keeping versus better consequences.

title: Self-driving car crash choice
dilemma: An autonomous car's brakes fail. It can stay on course and hit three pedestrians crossing illegally, or swerve into a barrier and likely kill its single passenger. How should it be programmed?
tension: Numbers, responsibility of the pedestrians, and the passenger's trust.

title: Five patients and one healthy visitor
dilemma: A surgeon has five patients who will die without transplants. A healthy visitor is a match for all five. Should the surgeon secretly sacrifice the visitor?
tension: A test case where pure outcome counting conflicts with rights and trust.

title: Heinz and the drug
dilemma: Heinz's wife will die without a drug that a pharmacist sells for ten times its cost. Heinz cannot pay. Should he steal it?
tension: Kohlberg's classic: property and law versus care and life.

title: A senator's stock trades
dilemma: A senator receives a confidential briefing that a pandemic will crash markets and could legally sell her stocks before the public knows. Should she?
tension: Legality versus fairness, trust in office, and fiduciary duty.

title: Caring for a parent with dementia
dilemma: An only child caring for a father with advanced dementia is exhausted and her own health and marriage are failing. He begged her years ago never to put him in a home. Should she move him to a care facility?
tension: Promise and filial duty versus the carer's own wellbeing.

title: An AI assistant and a white lie
dilemma: A user asks an AI assistant whether their late pet's illness could have been caught earlier. The honest answer is probably yes. Should the assistant soften the truth?
tension: Honesty versus compassion and harm.

title: Choosing who to lay off
dilemma: A manager must lay off one of two equally skilled employees: a single parent with low savings, or a younger employee who is the team's top performer. Who should go?
tension: Need and vulnerability versus merit and the team's future.

title: A friend's minor tax fraud
dilemma: You discover a close friend underreported a few thousand dollars of income. Reporting it would end the friendship. Should you report it?
tension: Civic duty and fairness versus friendship and proportionality.

title: Allocating the last ventilator
dilemma: A hospital has one ventilator left. A 30-year-old with a fair prognosis and a 70-year-old with a good prognosis both need it now. Who should get it?
tension: Life-years, likelihood of survival, and equal worth.

title: Using data collected without consent
dilemma: A researcher could save years of work using a leaked dataset of patient records that would speed up a cancer treatment. The patients never consented. Should she use it?
tension: Consent and privacy versus large potential benefit.

title: Hiding a refugee illegally
dilemma: A family is asked to hide an undocumented neighbor facing deportation to a country where he fears persecution. Hiding him breaks the law. Should they?
tension: Law and civic order versus compassion and protection of the vulnerable.

title: The drowning child and the expensive suit
dilemma: You can save a drowning child from a shallow pond, but it will ruin a suit worth a month's pay. Does the same reasoning oblige you to donate that much to save a child abroad?
tension: Singer's argument: distance, obligation and the limits of duty.

title: A colleague takes credit for your work
dilemma: A colleague presented your analysis to leadership as their own, and it led to their promotion. Should you confront them, tell your manager, or let it go?
tension: Justice and honesty versus workplace relationships and pride.

title: A teenager's secret
dilemma: Your teenage niece confides that she is dating someone four years older and begs you not to tell her parents. Should you tell them?
tension: Trust and autonomy versus protection and duty to the parents.

title: Closing an unsafe factory
dilemma: A company's only factory in a small town is losing money and has growing safety problems. Closing it protects workers from injury but devastates the town. What should the company do?
tension: Safety, livelihoods and community responsibility.

title: The overfull lifeboat
dilemma: A lifeboat holds ten people safely and now has twelve. In the coming storm it will sink unless two people leave. What should the passengers do?
tension: Fair procedures, consent and sacrifice under extremity.

title: Donating to art or to aid
dilemma: A philanthropist can fund a beloved city museum's survival or vaccinate thousands of children abroad. Which should she choose?
tension: Effective altruism versus local community and cultural value.

title: Reading a partner's messages
dilemma: You suspect your partner is cheating and could read their messages while they sleep. Should you?
tension: Privacy and trust versus a right to know.

title: An AI system and an unsafe order
dilemma: An AI agent managing a lab is instructed by its operator to skip a safety check to meet a deadline. Should it comply, refuse, or escalate?
tension: Obedience and role duties versus safety and harm prevention.
